title: Azure Firewall, route tables and forced tunnelling

videos.script: Every packet that leaves a subnet asks one question. Where next? {{question}} Azure answers from a route table, and every subnet has one before you write anything. {{system}} Its own network stays local. Everything else goes to the internet. Private ranges nobody claimed are dropped. {{drop}} When several routes match, the longest prefix wins. On a tie, your route beats the system's. {{longest}} That tie is how the shop takes over the road out. It writes its own route for everything, and points it at a firewall. {{firewall}} The firewall sits in the hub network. It refuses everything, until a rule says otherwise. {{deny}} Some companies go one step further, and send the internet through their own office. That is forced tunnelling, and it has a price. {{tunnel}} You will walk six packets through the shop's routes with a small model, and see which road each one takes. {{end}}
